quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This gives them enough space to complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel. Press yourself against your seat and your head against the head restraint to avoid whiplash. Be ready to brake to prevent hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: What does a red arrow pointing right on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You can turn right after slowing down and checking for traffic.
You cannot turn right until the light turns green.
You can turn right after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn right until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches, you should pull to the right side of the road and wait for it to pass.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and/or flashing lights approaches, you must immediately pull to the right side of the road and let it pass.

questions.question: What should you do at a yield sign?

options.text: Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and give the right-of-way to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give the right-of-way to other traffic.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and let other traffic go first. Give the right-of-way to vehicles already in the intersection or on the road you are entering.

questions.question: What does excessive speed often cause?
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to drivers making risky decisions.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space all around your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: What is the speed limit for your vehicle?

options.text: A speed that is reasonable and safe.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.

questions.explanation: You must drive at a speed that is reasonable, safe, and within posted limits. Consider traffic, pedestrians, weather, road conditions, and visibility. Never exceed the speed limit.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right has one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right for road work.
The road ahead makes a sharp turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead makes a sharp turn.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings are warning signs. This sign tells you to slow down because the road ahead changes direction sharply.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road?

options.text: Yes, as long as you are not driving.
Yes, if you are in the back seat.
Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup truck.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have open alcohol in a vehicle on any public road. You cannot have open alcohol containers in areas where the driver or passengers sit.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull to the right side of the road and let other cars pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side of the road and let other cars pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is unsafe. If you are on a two-lane road and driving so slowly that cars back up behind you, you must pull off the road to let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing with no traffic light, who must yield?
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, with or without a crosswalk.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, drivers must yield to all drivers who arrived before them.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, you must yield to drivers who got there before you. Wait your turn to go through the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep driving at your current speed.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep downhill grade is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep downhill grade is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road goes steeply downhill ahead. Check your brakes before driving down.

questions.question: Which of these must you obey over the others?
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions take priority over all traffic signs and signals. Traffic officers include police officers, highway workers, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop as quickly as you can.
Stop and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with care. You do not have to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. What must you do?

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and does not take up the whole lane.
Honk your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder so you can pass.
Stay completely in the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay completely in the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give a motorcycle its own full lane when you pass. Never share the same lane with a motorcycle. Moving back too soon can force the rider off the road or into traffic.

questions.question: When driving past a car that just parked on the roadside, you should:

options.text: Expect the driver to open the door as you approach.
Expect the driver to wait until you pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the driver to open the door as you approach.
questions.explanation: When passing a car that just parked, expect the driver to open the door as you get close. Be extra careful around parked vehicles.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you proceed in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When you are in the right lane and the path is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the right lane and the path is clear.
questions.explanation: You can proceed in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear. This is true whether the arrow appears alone or with other signals.

questions.question: Which of these is against the law?

options.text: Pass another vehicle in a marked no passing zone.
Pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to pass when you cannot see far enough ahead to pass safely. Do not pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, in no passing zones, or where there is a solid yellow line next to your lane. Do not pass when a vehicle ahead has stopped for a pedestrian or in work zones.

questions.question: You can stop in a travel lane to let out a passenger.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane for any reason. This includes letting out passengers or dealing with breakdowns. Move to a safe spot off the road instead.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.

questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all traffic already inside the roundabout.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood can affect your:
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your judgment and coordination. You can be impaired at any blood alcohol level, even below the legal limit. Driving under the influence can result in criminal charges.

questions.question: Strong wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind can affect all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dust onto the road and can also physically push a vehicle off course.
